test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 04 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In the context of Privatisation, what is the meaning of total decentralisation?

options.text: It implies 100% transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to private sector.
It implies 51% transfer of ownership of a private enterprise to public sector.
It implies 51% transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to private sector.
It implies 100% transfer of ownership of a private enterprise to public sector.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It implies 100% transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to private sector.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Privatisation** is the process of involving the **private sector** in the ownership or operation of a **state-owned enterprise**. It can take several forms, ranging from partial **disinvestment** to complete **denationalization**.
 
• In the context of the question, **total decentralisation** (or total privatisation) refers to the **100% transfer** of **ownership** and **management control** of a **public sector enterprise** to **private hands**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The transfer of ownership from a **private enterprise** to the **public sector** is known as **Nationalisation**. If **51%** or more is transferred to the government, the government gains **majority control**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The transfer of **51% ownership** of a **public enterprise** to the **private sector** is known as **Strategic Disinvestment** or **Majority Privatisation**. In this case, the government might still hold a minority stake, but management control is usually transferred. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• A **100% transfer** of a **private enterprise** to the **public sector** is the absolute form of **Nationalisation**, where the **state** takes full **monopoly** over the industry or specific firm. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The ultimate goal of **total privatisation** is to remove **government interference** entirely from the commercial operations of the entity, allowing **market forces** to dictate efficiency and pricing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **LPG Reforms (1991):** India introduced **Privatisation** as part of the **New Economic Policy** in **July 1991**. The **Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation (LPG)** model was launched by then-Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh** to address the **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis.
 
• **Disinvestment:** This refers to the **dilution** of the **Government of India's** stake in **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)**. It is categorized into **Minority Disinvestment** (where the government retains **51%** or more stake) and **Strategic Disinvestment** (where the government sells a significant portion, often **50%** or more, and transfers management control).
 
• **DIPAM:** The **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management**, under the **Ministry of Finance**, is the nodal agency responsible for managing **government investments** in **equity** and advising on the **disinvestment** process.
 
• **Modes of Privatisation:**
 
 
• **Denationalization:** Total **100% transfer** of ownership.
 
• **Joint Venture:** Partial transfer where both **public** and **private** sectors co-exist.
 
• **Franchising:** The government grants the right to a private firm to provide a specific service for a **fixed period**.
 
 
 
• **Objectives:** The primary motives include **improving financial discipline**, facilitating **modernization**, reducing the **fiscal burden** on the **Exchequer**, and promoting **consumer-centric** services through healthy **competition**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Navratnas and Maharatnas:** To ensure that **PSUs** can compete even without full privatisation, the government granted **financial autonomy** to certain profit-making enterprises. **Maharatna** status, introduced in **2010**, gives the highest level of **investment freedom** (up to **5,000 crore**) to top-performing companies like **ONGC**, **NTPC**, and **SAIL**.
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956:** Before **1991**, India followed a policy of **expansion** of the **public sector**, where **17 industries** were exclusively reserved for the **state**. The **1991 reforms** drastically reduced this number to encourage **private participation**.
 
• **Global Context:** Mass **privatisation** gained global momentum in the **1980s**, famously known as **Thatcherism** in the **United Kingdom**, which sought to reduce **state role** in the **economy** to improve **GDP growth** and **productivity**.
